questions.q_en: The Kalbeliya dance, recognized by UNESCO, is traditionally performed by which group in Rajasthan?

• Meena: Participate in Bhavai, a balancing dance involving brass pitchers.

• Gujjar: Known for performing Chari dance in the Kishangarh region.

Further Insight:

• Rajasthan

○ Ghoomar - Performed by women, originally a Bhil tribe dance

○ Jhulan Leela

○ Chari - Symbolizes joy and ritual of collecting water in pots, performed by Saini and Gujjar communities

○ Ghapal

○ Suisini

○ Ganagor

○ Jhuma

○ Bhavai - Performed by Jat, Meena, Bhil, and Kalbelia tribes

○ Panihari - Associated with women fetching water

○ Kalbeliya - Performed by Kalbeliya tribe, UNESCO intangible cultural heritage

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding Bharatanatyam:

a. Bharatanatyam originated in the state of Tamil Nadu and is traditionally associated with the temples.

b. The dance form includes elements of Tandava, symbolizing masculine energy.

c. Bharatanatyam is performed exclusively by female dancers in the modern era.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu and is deeply rooted in temple culture.

• Bharatanatyam incorporates both Tandava (masculine) and Lasya (feminine) elements.

• Bharatanatyam is performed by both male and female dancers in modern times.

Further Insight:

• Bharatanatyam

○ State in which it perfomed: Tamil Nadu

○ History and facts:

■ Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India, originating in the temples of Tamil Nadu.

■ It was traditionally performed by devadasis (temple dancers) as a form of devotion to deities.

■ It was codified in the Natya Shastra by the sage Bharata.

■ The revival of Bharatanatyam in the 20th century was largely due to the efforts of Rukmini Devi Arundale, who brought it from temples to the proscenium stage, refining its aesthetics and removing any associations with the devadasi system.

○ Exponents:

■ Rukmini Devi Arundale

■ Padma Subrahmanyam

■ Vyjayanthimala

■ Padmini

■ Smt. Swati Daithankar

Further Insight:

• Kuchipudi

○ State in which it performed: Andhra Pradesh

○ History and facts:

■ Kuchipudi originates from the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh.

■ It began as a form of dance-drama and has roots in the Natya Shastra, similar to Bharatanatyam.

■ Historically, it was performed by male Brahmin performers in temples as part of religious rituals, but it has evolved to include female performers.

■ Kuchipudi is known for its graceful movements, use of speech, and dramatic storytelling.

■ Deepa Shashindran
